A1.justification: Both PDFs describe COMIC, with the same title, authors, research problem, and core framework. The text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–H are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original causal-direction experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmarks, including Table 1 and the ablations in Appendix G.

after.justification: V4 reports original benchmark results in Table 1 and Figures 1–2, together with width, hyperprior, and cause-encoding experiments in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The stated training procedure now includes MAP pretraining before variational optimization. Appendix B changes fixed unit-variance bias priors to priors with optimized scale hyperparameters, and Appendix D replaces the softplus output-scale link with an exponential link. These materially revise the model and optimization procedure, although the core codelength-based decision rule remains.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 12 synthetic benchmarks and the same real-world Tübingen cause-effect task, including the existing confounded and low-noise scenarios. Appendix H remains a discussion of possible multivariate extensions, without multivariate experiments.

E2.justification: V4 removes both post-hoc independence-testing comparators, RESIT and LOCI-HSIC, from Figure 1 and Table 1, substantially narrowing that part of the comparison. Its remaining LOCI comparator is v1's LOCI-Likelihood under a shorter name. The other baseline variants are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix D changes the default hidden width from 20 to 50, variational training from 1,000 to 2,500 epochs, and KL warm-up from 100 to 250 epochs. A constant learning rate of 0.01 becomes a cosine schedule between 0.01 and 0.000001, and v4 specifies 2,500 MAP-pretraining epochs. These are substantial reported configuration changes; benchmark sampling and per-dataset metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix G removes the location-scale versus location-only ablation, the model-complexity objective ablation, and the network-depth study. It also drops width 500 and both uniform cause-encoding alternatives. Width, hyperprior/pruning, and Gaussian-versus-VB-GMM analyses remain with revised results; v1 Tables 4–5 correspond to v4 Tables 3–4.

E5.justification: V4 adds across-benchmark means and standard deviations in Table 1 and Figure 2. These describe variation across datasets, not uncertainty across repeated runs. It removes v1's Appendix D statement that repeated experiments showed negligible differences and therefore needed no error bars. Neither version specifies run counts or seeds.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces many COMIC results under the revised configuration: SIM accuracy/Bi-AUROC changes from 0.90/0.97 to 0.57/0.58, and Tübingen from 0.87/0.97 to 0.67/0.75. These are not same-setting performance comparisons. Retained baseline values are unchanged. V4 adds overall summaries placing COMIC second behind GPLVM, and extensively revises the retained ablation results.

T1.justification: Appendix B generalizes the bias-prior variance in Equation 24 and includes its scale in hyperparameter optimization. Appendix C correspondingly replaces unit bias contributions in the GP covariance derivations with bias variances. The principal definitions, Proposition 4.2, Corollary 4.3, and overall proof strategy remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retreat from broad superiority over complexity-based and regression-based approaches to improvements over most methods on several benchmarks. The results narrative now acknowledges GPLVM's best overall performance and describes COMIC as comparable to several methods on Tübingen, replacing the earlier strong superiority claims. The methodological and identifiability contributions remain.

C2.justification: V4 removes explanations connecting near-ideal Bi-AUROC and strong performance on difficult or confounded data to COMIC's flexibility and prediction confidence. It emphasizes marginal- versus maximum-likelihood objectives and explains GPLVM's stronger results alongside its computational demands. Appendix G revises interpretations of width sensitivity and hyperprior usefulness. The existing non-convexity and Gaussian-marginal limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix D substantially revises the reproducible training recipe, including scheduler bounds and the MAP-pretraining objective and duration. V4 also removes the COMIC repository pointer, the explicit GAM specification for CAM, and the VB-GMM maximum of 50 components. Hardware descriptions and the remaining baseline and dataset access pointers are retained; the PDFs do not establish any change in actual repository availability.

R1.justification: The related-work section and cited-work inventory remain unchanged apart from bibliographic formatting. Research positioning shifts modestly toward comparison with maximum-likelihood objectives and toward presenting GPLVM as a stronger but more computationally demanding alternative.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in the abstract, contribution statements, results discussion, conclusion, and shortened ablation narrative. V4 adds an explicit Limitations & Future Work label. The overall section and appendix organization, and most methodological and theoretical exposition, remain intact.

P2.justification: V4 adds an overall-performance bar chart with error bars as Figure 2, while removing v1's two ablation figures and depth-study table. Table 1 gains an Overall column and second-place formatting while losing comparator rows; the width and cause-encoding tables also lose rows. Figure 1's comparator legends and caption are revised. These extend beyond numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: V4 provides a useful overall-performance summary and more qualified claims, but removes direct tests of the location-scale component and model-complexity objective, along with the depth study and COMIC code-access pointer. These losses weaken support for central design choices and reduce reproducibility information, outweighing the limited reporting gains. The judgment rests on those evidence and documentation losses, rather than the lower scores obtained under changed settings.
